title: The Last Clock
premise: In the winter of 1893, widowed lighthouse keeper Bram Ashgrove tends the light above a dying Cornish fishing village, keeping fifteen years of careful silences about her late husband's secret work as a clockmaker-for-hire. When a sealed letter arrives naming his family as unwitting couriers in a smuggling ring that has already killed one man, Bram must finish the intricate regulator clock he left incomplete — the only proof of who ordered the deaths. As storms cut off the coast and the smugglers close in, she must choose between destroying the evidence to protect her daughter and finishing it to honor the truth. She completes the clock, exposes the ring at terrible cost, and learns that some silences were never meant to keep people safe — only to keep her alone.
about_author: B. M. Nystrom is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs and coastal trade records from the Victorian era. They write historical fiction from a converted net loft on the Cornish coast.

chapters.title: The Light and the Silence
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A brutal November storm batters the lighthouse while Bram keeps the light burning and reflects on fifteen years of widowhood and practiced silence. Her daughter Wren finds an unopened letter in her father's old sea chest. The beat is quiet dread: the past knocking at a door Bram sealed long ago.

chapters.title: A Letter Sealed in Wax
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The letter names the Ashgrove family as couriers in a smuggling operation and demands delivery of 'the finished work' within weeks. Bram discovers her husband's hidden workshop beneath the boathouse, containing an unfinished regulator clock. Emotional beat: betrayal — the man she mourned had a whole second life.

chapters.title: What the Workshop Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren explores the workshop behind her mother's back, finding ledgers, coded notes, and a photograph of her father with three strangers. She begins to understand her mother's silences differently. Beat: adolescent anger curdling into fascination — she wants to know her father more than she wants to be safe.

chapters.title: The Man from Penzance
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A stranger arrives claiming to be a shipping agent, asking pointed questions about deliveries. Bram lies smoothly — too smoothly — and realizes how good she's become at it. That night she finds the first gear-train component missing from the workshop. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; someone else wants the clock finished.

chapters.title: Gears in the Dark
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram teaches herself her husband's craft from his notebooks, working by lamplight after her shifts. Flashbacks reveal their marriage: love, yes, but also things he never told her. Beat: grief transmuted into intimacy — she comes to know him better dead than alive.

chapters.title: The Drowned Courier
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A body washes up near the cove — the third stranger from the photograph. Wren recognizes him and says nothing to her mother, hiding the man's notebook instead. Beat: loyalty vs. truth begins its real war inside the family; Wren now holds a silence of her own.

chapters.title: Storm Glass Falling
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The great storm of the year descends; the village evacuates inland but Bram cannot leave the light. The stranger returns with men, demanding the clock. Bram bargains for time using the storm itself. Beat: duty crystallizes — the light must burn, whatever else burns with it.

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Trapped together by the storm, Bram and Wren finally exchange their secrets: the letter, the notebook, the lies. Rage, then reckoning. They finish the clock side by side through the worst night of the year. Beat: love against duty resolved into partnership — truth spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: What the Clock Proved
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The finished regulator's hidden compartment yields the ledger naming the ring's leader: a respected harbormaster. Bram delivers the clock and testimony to the customs officer in Falmouth, knowing it will ruin friends and neighbors alike. Beat: the price of survival paid in full — truth costs everything she built her life on.

chapters.title: Keeping the Light
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, spring. The harbormaster is tried; the village heals unevenly. Bram keeps the lighthouse, and the clock now chimes in the keeper's cottage — honest time at last. Wren chooses to stay. Final beat: quiet peace earned, not given; Bram learns that ending a silence was the truest act of keeping anyone safe.
